newsitem.title: USA: Kennecott build-up to prompt copper concs juggling.
newsitem.headline: Kennecott build-up to prompt copper concs juggling.

text.p: Bringing Kennecott's $850 million copper smelter up to speed by mid-year will prompt a juggling of raw material supply for rival refineries, traders and producers said.
"Basically in the (U.S.) southwest there will be less local raw materials available, and we will probably need more concentrate imports," a copper concentrate official at one U.S. producer noted.
A sales manager for another producer added, "The units that they are producing are hitting the market. They just may not be in refined form, but in every other form."

A trader noted, "It changes the formula for everyone else. The whole delivery picture for metal will change. There will be more refined metal delivered in the southwest and it has got to go somewhere."
Earlier on Thursday RTZ-CRA said its glitch-hit new smelter Kennecott Utah Copper in Bingham Canyon was expected to be fully operational by about June.

Problems at the 270,000 tonnes per year plant cost RTZ $150 million in lost profit after a delay of well over a year to reach full capacity. The smelter operated at 51 percent of design capacity at the end of the fourth quarter.

Kennecott has been selling its surplus matte and concentrate to other producers such as Phelps Dodge, BHP Coppper, Cyprus Amax, or ASARCO for refining, industry sources said. Traders also bought some material.
Industry sources said they were not too concerned about any huge stockpiles of raw materials at the smelter.
A Kennecott spokeswoman said there was 66,000 short tons of contained copper in blister, concentrate, matte and scrap stocked at the smelter.

"I don't think the other producers will have to scramble once Kennecott is back on because there are other raw materials out there such as scrap, but eventually some of those producers will have to start being net buyers (of concentrates)," a trader said.

There was ample supply of concentrate at present with the spot market quiet. Most of the long-term contracts for this year have been signed with topping up from spot deals not expected until the second half of the year.
For producers such as BHP and Phelps Dodge who have huge mining operations, it will be a matter of swaps rather than becoming a net buyer, industry sources said.

But there was still some skepticism among rival producers and traders about Kennecott's certainty of reaching full output by mid-year. The smelter will be partially shut down for six weeks in from early April for further modification.
Nevertheless, Richard de J Osborne, ASARCO's chairman, president and chief executive told reporters earlier this month he was confident that problems at Kennecott will be sorted out.
Once Kennecott cranks up to full capacity, observers expected stocks of intermediate raw materials at the smelter site to be wound down.
Meanwhile the U.S. copper demand remains strong with no signs of softening. "The U.S. is definitely the star of the market," a physical merchant said.
Premiums were sold at just under 3.00 cents per pound over spot COMEX. Spot March was trading at about 114.00 cents a pound midday.
